title: Three Spins and a Line
logline: Alone on a floodlit pitch at nine at night, a young player misses a shot against a goalkeeper they imagined out of chalk. One line drawn on the ball shows the spin behind every fix: a slow backward roll for the laces drive, sideways for the curler, forward for the volley, backward for the bonus chip, and almost none for a knuckleball teaser. Each chapter ends with body cues, the classic mistake and a solo drill for the next practice, and the bonus chip gets its own practice card.

characters.name: Tavi (the player, spoken to only as 'you')
characters.design: Right-footed 14-year-old, about 5.5 heads tall, built only from rounded rectangles and circles (corner radius at least 15% of the short side, no outlines). Teal shirt #3FE0D0 with darker teal shade shapes and one orange chest band #FF7A3D that rhymes with the line on the ball. Shorts #232B5C, teal socks, chalk-white boots #F4F1E8 with a pale lace zone. Warm brown skin #A0673F with one shade #7E4E2F. Rounded cloud-tuft hair in #232B5C. Two oval eyes #151A3D and a small mouth dash. Eyes grow 10% for surprise. Rig: 2-bone IK arms and legs, pelvis turn, spine lean. Idle breathing loop 2-4 px, 3 s. Keyed poses: idle, walk, drop_ball, draw_line, approach, plant, backswing, whip, contact_drive, follow_through, lean_back, curl_wipe, thigh_lift, volley_set, volley_contact, chip_stab, knuckle_stab, shout, fist_out, shrug, pick_up_walk.
characters.role: The viewer's stand-in. The narrator never says the name. Tavi misses the first shot, solves one problem per chapter, shows every mistake, fix and drill, and replays the first shot correctly at the end.

characters.name: Chalk (the imagined goalkeeper)
characters.design: Tall capsule-shaped keeper made of pitch paint. Chalk white #F4F1E8 with one pale shade tone and a faint 3% dusty grain. Huge rounded mitten gloves. Two dot eyes #151A3D and short eyebrow dashes that carry every expression. No outlines, no mouth. He builds out of the goal line: the line lifts (trim path), folds and morphs into his body. At the end he sinks back into it. Each move gives off 8-12 chalk-dust particles. Poses: rise, ready, arms_crossed, reach_big, dive_left, dive_right, punch_clear, catch, rush_out, draw_wall, shuffle, lean_wrong, confused, squint, sink.
characters.role: The deadpan problem-setter. He never speaks and he learns after each goal. Chapter 1: he stands big in the middle. Chapter 2: he draws a chalk wall and guards the near post. Chapter 3: he punches the ball clear, then rushes out for the chip. Teaser: he cannot read the knuckleball at all.

characters.name: The Ball and its Line (motif)
characters.design: Orange ball #FF7A3D in every palette, with a darker crescent shade and a light rim on the lit edge. Tavi draws one chalk-white line around it in the cold open. The line is a true 3D great circle, projected every frame from the spin state, so every kind of spin reads on screen: slow backward roll (drive), sideways turn that is anticlockwise seen from above, with the front edge swinging left (curler), forward roll (volley), faster backward roll on a slow ball (chip), almost still (knuckleball). The ball squashes on contact. A ghost variant is a dashed outline at 40% with no line.
characters.role: The motif. Planted in the cold open ('Remember that line'), it shows the spin in every chapter. It pays off in the ending ('It told you everything') and in the teaser, where the line hardly turns.

characters.name: The Air Crowd
characters.design: Tiny round particles with two dot eyes, #7FB8FF in the X-ray palette and #F4FBFF in the Open Sky palette. They move in streams. Small #FF4FA3 puffs pop where they bump into each other. Faces show only in close-ups. In wide shots they are plain moving dashes.
characters.role: The metaphor for air. The crowd rushes past the ball, gets thrown aside by a spinning ball and shoves back. Used for sideways spin, the forward-spin dive, the chip float and the knuckleball flag.

component_kit.name: Props
component_kit.props: { kind: 'chalkWall'|'disc'|'flag'|'cone'|'bag'|'tape'|'targetBox'; x:number; y:number; build?:number; crumble?:number; count?:number; height?:number; text?:string }

component_kit.name: Ball
component_kit.props: { radiusPx:number; spinAxis:[number,number,number]; spinRps:number; timeScale:number; phase:number; squash?: {amount:number; dir:number}; line:boolean; ghost?: boolean; arrows?: 'none'|'spin'; arrowColor?: string }
component_kit.notes: #FF7A3D in every palette, with a crescent shade and a rim light. The line is a 3D great circle projected every frame from the spin state. Its plane sits 60 deg off the spin axis, so any spin shows. Use the same spinAxis as the FlightSim shot. The curler reads anticlockwise seen from above (front edge swings left). Never describe it as a clock hand. At 30 fps, show fast spin only at timeScale 1/10 or slower, to avoid strobing. Ghost: dashed outline at 40%, no line. Spin arrows are lime #B6F24A, or blue #4A93E6 (chip) and orange (volley) in the mirror.

component_kit.name: FlightSim
component_kit.props: { name: string; v0:number; elevDeg:number; azimDeg:number; z0?:number; spinRps:number; spinAxis:[number,number,number]; cd:number; clFixed?:number; spinPush?: boolean; sideForce?: {peakN:number; wavelengthM:number; phase:number}; stopAt: 'goalLine'|'ground'|number; startFrame:number; slowMo?:number }
component_kit.notes: useFlight hook. Point mass 0.43 kg, radius 0.11 m, air 1.2 kg/m3, area 0.038 m2, gravity 9.81. Ball on the ground starts at z0 0.11 m. Air brake = 0.5*rho*A*Cd*v^2 against the velocity. Spin push = 0.5*rho*A*Cl*v^2 along unit(spinAxis x velocity), with Cl = min(0.35, 0.5*sqrt(r*omega/v)) unless clFixed is set. Spin decays 2%/s. sideForce (knuckle only) is a sine along the path. Integrate at dt 1/600 s and sample at 60 fps. Axis vectors, for a shot a degrees right of +x (heading (cos a, -sin a, 0)): backspin = -(sin a, cos a, 0), topspin = +(sin a, cos a, 0). Per shot: MISS, DRIVE_WALL, CHIP, CHIP_GHOST [0,-1,0]; DRIVE_R and TOE_HIT (a 8.5) [-0.148,-0.989,0]; DRIVE_L (a -8.5) [0.148,-0.989,0]; VOLLEY (a 10) [0.174,0.985,0]; CURLER (a 8) = 0.891 x [0,0,1] - 0.454 x (sin 8, cos 8, 0) = [-0.063,-0.450,0.891]; CURLER_AIM_MISS (a 0) [0,-0.454,0.891]. Named shots: MISS, DRIVE_R, DRIVE_L, DRIVE_WALL, TOE_HIT, CURLER, CURLER_AIM_MISS, DROP, VOLLEY, VOLLEY_GHOST, EASY, SMASH, BOUNCE_DRILL, CHIP, CHIP_GHOST, KNUCKLE (values in each scene; all checks were run again in this model). Precompute every shot to JSON in a build step. A validator checks each scene's stated values (height at the line within 0.1 m, side position within 0.1 m, time within 0.05 s). It also checks the signs: backspin pushes up, VOLLEY pushes down and CURLER pushes toward +y (left). So calculateMetadata never throws. The ball in flight moves on linear time with no design ease. Slow motion only when labelled.

component_kit.name: Trajectory
component_kit.props: { samples: Vec3[]; progress:number; style: 'solid'|'dotted'|'ghost'; color:string; view: 'side'|'top'|'pov'; startLine?: boolean; brackets?: {atM:number; label?:string}[]; circle?: boolean; highlight?: {fromM:number; toM:number} }
component_kit.notes: Draws a sim path with @remotion/paths evolvePath. Ghosts at 30%. startLine draws the dashed launch line. Brackets measure the gap or dip from the samples and are never typed by hand. circle extends a curler into its full faint circle at true scale. highlight glows part of a path (the second half in s11). This replaces the separate aim guide.

component_kit.name: XRayLeg
component_kit.props: { view: 'side'|'top'|'behind'; mode: 'whip'|'contact'|'ankle'|'curl'|'volley'|'chip'|'knuckle'; ankle: 'locked'|'loose'; toes: 'down'|'up'; contact: 'mid-laces'|'toe'|'inside-right-of-centre'|'low'|'centre'; timeScale:number; glow?: {thigh?:number; shin?:number}; tags?: {joint:'knee'|'toe'; text:string; icon:'bike'|'car'}[]; morph?: 'whip'|'hammer'|'racket'; mirror?: boolean }
component_kit.notes: Bones glow #C9F6FF, soft tissue #2A7F8F at 40-60%, active muscle #FF4FA3. A loose ankle gives toward more toes-down, the true direction, and costs only a little speed. Morphs use interpolatePath between matched point counts: whip, loose-headed hammer, tennis racket. The curl wipe moves forward and to the right, toward the aim-off flag, and drags the back of the ball to the right.

component_kit.name: AirFlow
component_kit.props: { mode: 'top'|'side'; flowSpeed:number; particles:number; faces?: boolean; coat?: boolean; spinDir:number; hugSide?: 'left'|'right'|'top'|'bottom'; wakeAngleDeg:number; bumpPuffs?: boolean; flap?: {ampDeg:number; hz:number}; seed:number }
component_kit.notes: The Air Crowd, 300-400 particles. #7FB8FF in X-ray, #F4FBFF in Open Sky. faces adds two dot eyes for close-ups. Bump puffs #FF4FA3. Top views put the flight toward the top of the frame, so the with-flow side of an anticlockwise ball is screen-left. Sideways spin: the side moving with the flow holds it longer, the wake swings the other way, and the ball moves toward the with-flow side. Forward spin: flick up, push down. Backward spin: flick down, push up. Knuckle: the wake flaps like a flag.

component_kit.name: ForceArrow
component_kit.props: { origin: [number,number]; angleDeg:number; lengthRatio:number; color:string; label?: 'weight'|'side push'|'float'|'dive'|'air' }
component_kit.notes: lengthRatio 1 = ball weight. The shaft draws in 24 frames, the head pops in 8 (easeOutBack), the label pops 5 frames later. Plain-word labels only. Lengths follow the verified ratios: side push about 1/2, volley dive about 1/3, chip float about 1/4.

component_kit.name: HUD
component_kit.props: { kind: 'stopwatch'|'tag'|'bars'|'counter'|'dots'|'timeline'|'meter'; value?:number; unit?:string; icon?:string; bars?: {label:string; value:number; color:string}[]; dots?: {total:507; lit:96; cols:39}; showDigits?: boolean; font: 'JetBrains Mono'|'Barlow Condensed'|'Space Grotesk' }
component_kit.notes: Counting digits in JetBrains Mono so they do not jitter. Only verified numbers, always with '≈'. The contact stopwatch stops at 0.009 s in s02. The s04 speed tag reads '≈ 67 km/h' with '≈ 42 mph' under it (club players, age 12), on a ghost ball beside Tavi. bars cover foot vs ball, speed vs spin and the '-15% (toe hit)' bar. dots is the volley goal share (visual only in s13) and needs its source caption. meter is the top-of-bounce hover meter and the drill power meter.

component_kit.name: MetaphorInset
component_kit.notes: A rounded card with one small parametric SVG per metaphor, 6 rounded shapes or fewer. Each metaphor appears once, then a cut back to the pitch shows the payoff. The trolley is about four times the ball's weight, so the ball leaves only a little faster. The same drawings serve as mini icons on the PracticeBoard and HUD tags.

component_kit.name: ChapterCard
component_kit.props: { variant: 'title'|'chapter'|'spinRow'|'end'; index?:number; title?:string; subtitle?:string; surface: 'grass'|'sky'; writeOnFrames:number; slots?: {spin:'slow'|'side'|'forward'|'back'|'none'|'?'; icon:string}[] }
component_kit.notes: Chalk letters #F4F1E8 in Rubik 800 (96-120 px), underline #FF7A3D, glow #FFD166, written on the grass like pitch paint. Chapter subtitles: 'slow spin', 'sideways spin', 'forward spin'. spinRow draws the ending's chalk boxes with a Ball in each. Entrance 0.4-0.5 s decelerate, exit 0.2-0.3 s accelerate. No Nexa, no Montserrat, no copied layout.

component_kit.name: Caption
component_kit.notes: 4 words max for labels. Nunito 700 for labels, Atkinson Hyperlegible for notes and sources. Soft pop: spring stiffness 120, damping 14. Snappy: stiffness 300, damping 20. No technical terms in any label. Real terms appear only on a WordCard.

component_kit.name: PracticeBoard
component_kit.props: { cues?: {icon:string; text:string}[]; mistake?: string; fix?: string; drill?: {text:string; icon:string}; safety?: string; note?: string; activeIndex:number; layout: 'board'|'stamp' }
component_kit.notes: One layout for every practical beat, so viewers learn the 'use this' moment. 3 cues max. Stamps: MISTAKE #FF4FA3, FIX #3FE0D0, DRILL #FFD166, CUE #F4F1E8, 8-frame pop with overshoot. activeIndex follows word timestamps. Wall drills (s07, s18) show: 'Solid wall, no windows. Nobody near the wall. Pick a spot far from roads and parked cars. Jog and pass easy for 5 minutes. Start at half power.' Goal drills (s12, the rope-on-a-goal option in s07 and the chip card in s20) show: 'Nobody in or behind the goal. Pick a spot far from roads and parked cars. Jog and pass easy for 5 minutes. Start at half power.' The drive board cues are 'Run-up at an angle', 'Hand-width beside ball' and 'Toes down, locked'. The volley board cues are 'Eyes on the ball', 'Arms out wide' and 'Knee over ball'. The drive board also shows the note 'No wall? Tie a rope across a goal at knee height.'

component_kit.name: SplitScreen
component_kit.props: { left: ReactNode; right: ReactNode; divider:number; merge:number; dial?: number }
component_kit.notes: The divider draws with a trim path. merge (0-1) slides both halves into one ball. dial runs -1 (backward, float) to +1 (forward, dive) and swaps the spin arrows and paths between CHIP and VOLLEY. Chip on the left, volley on the right.

component_kit.name: WordCard
component_kit.props: { term: string; meaning: string; anchor: [number,number]; holdFrames: number; icon?: 'arrowBack'|'arrowForward'|'boot'|'spinPush' }
component_kit.notes: The one place a real term appears on screen. It pops on the term's word timestamp with the snappy spring. Chalk card #F4F1E8 on a soft #151A3D plate. Term in Rubik 800 with the orange underline #FF7A3D, plain meaning under it in Nunito 700. Hold 2-2.5 s, then shrink to a small chip in the frame corner. Used once per learn-word, at its first use: instep (s05), backspin (s06), Magnus effect (s10), topspin (s16). Spin words describe how the top of the ball turns. Caption labels stay plain words.

learn_words.meaning: the laces part of your foot, not the inside
the top of the ball turns back toward you as it flies
the spin push: air shoves a spinning ball sideways, up or down
the top of the ball turns toward the goal as it flies

scenes.narration: Nine at night. An empty pitch. <short pause> Just you, one ball, and a keeper in your head. His name is Chalk. <short pause> You draw one line around the ball. Remember that line. <short pause> You shoot. <long pause> Over the bar. <short pause> You shout at it. It doesn't listen. <short pause> Chalk doesn't even move.
visual_beats: [1 s silent pre-roll] Dark sky #151A3D with a 3-layer star field. Four floodlights clunk on one after another. Each blooms 4 glow rings in 0.4 s.
'Nine at night.' Slow push (easeInOutSine, 8% over 5 s) past the stand. The stand clock shows nine.
'An empty pitch.' Wide side view in 4 parallax layers (0.2x, 0.5x, 1x, 1.3x). Dust drifts in the light beams. Behind the goal: a low fence and a dark car park.
'Just you, one ball,' Tavi walks in from the left and drops the ball 18 m out. Two small sim bounces, then it settles.
'and a keeper in your head.' The goal-line paint peels up, folds and builds into Chalk (trim path 0.8 s, then morph). He blinks awake.
'His name is Chalk.' Chalk claps his mittens and a puff of chalk dust rises. Label 'CHALK' pops.
'You draw one line around the ball.' Top-down close-up: a marker draws one white line all the way round the orange ball (trim path, 30 frames).
'Remember that line.' The line glows once. Everything else dims by 20%.
'You shoot.' Side view. Three-step run-up from a slight angle, with a long last stride. The standing foot lands behind the ball. Tavi's chest stays behind the ball (lean_back). Contact.
[long pause] The ball climbs on the MISS sim. In a tracking close-up the line rolls backward. The camera tilts up after it.
'Over the bar.' The ball clears the bar by about half a metre and drops over the fence into the car park. A faint car alarm chirps once.
'You shout at it.' Speech bubble from Tavi: 'DOWN! DOWN!' (snappy pop).
'It doesn't listen.' The car alarm chirps again. The bubble shrinks away.
'Chalk doesn't even move.' The camera eases back to Chalk: arms crossed, one eyebrow up, feet exactly where they were.
scenes.transition_out: Zoom-through: the camera rushes back to the spot and into Tavi's boot at the contact frame. The frame freezes and s02 opens on it.
facts_used: No narrated numbers. Bar height 2.44 m in the sim comes from 'A full-size goal is 7.32 m wide and 2.44 m high' (chip safe list).
'clears the bar by about half a metre' (visual) is sim geometry: ball centre about 3.06 m, ball bottom about 2.95 m, bar 2.44 m.
scenes.physics_sim: MISS: start 18 m out, central, z0 0.11 m. 21 m/s (76 km/h), 18 deg up, 0 deg sideways. Backspin 5 rev/s, spinAxis [0,-1,0] (top of the ball turning back toward the kicker). Cd 0.25, Cl from the kit model (about 0.20 at launch, lift about 1.9 N). Checks: ball centre about 3.06 m high at the goal line after about 1.05 s (ball bottom about 2.95 m, so it clears the bar by about 0.5 m). Peak about 3.1 m. Lands about 30 m from the kick (12 m past the goal line) after about 1.9 s. Put the car park at that spot and fire the alarm on the landing frame. Control check for s20: the same launch with no spin crosses at about 1.25 m, under the bar.
sfx: floodlight clunk x4 with a rising electrical hum

scenes.narration: What went wrong? <short pause> Your foot touches the ball for about a hundredth of a second. After that, it's on its own. <short pause> Three kicks tonight, one idea: spin. How much, which way, or none at all. <short pause> By lights out, you'll score this shot.
visual_beats: 'What went wrong?' Rewind: the MISS sim plays backward. The ball drops out of the sky onto Tavi's boot.
'Your foot touches the ball for about a hundredth of a second.' Freeze at contact, the ball slightly squashed on the laces. HUD stopwatch (JetBrains Mono) creeps from 0.000 to 0.009 s.

'After that, it's on its own.' Unfreeze. A dotted tether between boot and ball snaps with a small spark. A fan of faint orange ghost paths (30%) sprays out from the contact point: low, curling, dipping, floating.
'Three kicks tonight,' Three paths brighten. Small icons tag them: laces, inside of foot, volley.
'one idea: spin.' A lime spin arrow draws around the ball and the line starts to turn.
'How much, which way,' The arrow speeds up, then flips its axis through four states: slow back, sideways, forward, back (0.5 s each).
'or none at all.' The arrow fades and the line almost stops. One beat of silence.
'By lights out, you'll score this shot.' The ghost fan fades. One dotted path (DRIVE_L preview) skims low into the bottom-left corner. A tiny floodlight icon in the frame corner blinks off once.
[2.5 s hold] The camera cranes up to top-down. The pitch markings slide into the title 'THREE SPINS AND A LINE' in chalk letters (Rubik 800) with an orange underline. Original title sting.
scenes.transition_out: The title letters slide back into pitch markings. The camera tilts down to the ball spot, where chalk writes chapter card 1 on the grass.
facts_used: 'about a hundredth of a second' <- 'Foot and ball touch for only about 9 thousandths of a second (9.1 ms at 1000 Hz, 9.12 ms at 4500 fps)' (drive) and 'In a real curve kick, the foot touches the ball for only about 10 thousandths of a second (9.6 to 12 ms, measured at 2500 frames per second)' (curler). 'About' holds for both.
Stopwatch stops at 0.009 s because the shot on screen is a laces kick (drive value, about 9 ms).
Cut for the word budget: 'That tiny moment decides everything.' The ghost fan now plays under 'After that, it's on its own.'
scenes.physics_sim: MISS samples in reverse. Ghost fan at 30%: DRIVE_R, CURLER, VOLLEY and CHIP, all redrawn from one contact point. Promise path: DRIVE_L samples, dotted.
sfx: soft shimmer as the ghost paths fan out
three light pops on the icons
spin whirr that changes pitch with each axis
soft blip as the floodlight icon blinks
original title sting, 2.5 s rising three-note figure

scenes.narration: Problem one: a shot Chalk can't reach. Low and hard. <short pause> Weird fact: after a clean strike, the ball can fly faster than your foot. How?
visual_beats: [1 s card] Chalk writes '1 · THE DRIVE' on the grass, subtitle 'slow spin'. The card's ball line rolls slowly backward.
'Problem one: a shot Chalk can't reach.' Chalk stands tall in the goal with arms wide. A pale reach bubble covers the middle of the goal.
'Low and hard.' Two small target boxes glow in the bottom corners, outside the bubble.
'Weird fact:' Side view of Tavi at the ball. A chalk '!' pops.

'after a clean strike, the ball can fly faster than your foot.' Slow-motion replay (tag 'SLOW MOTION'). HUD bars ride along: FOOT (teal) and BALL (orange). After contact the BALL bar passes the FOOT bar. No digits.
'How?' A big chalk question mark. Chalk peeks round the post and scratches his head. The camera starts its push toward the boot.
scenes.transition_out: Push into the boot. The boot turns see-through and the X-ray leg builds inside it (match morph, 1 s).
facts_used: No spoken number. 'faster than your foot' <- 'A skilled adult sends the ball about 1.35 times faster than the centre of the foot moves' and 'Strike quality rises with age: the ball/foot speed ratio goes from about 1.0 at U9 to 1.26 at U20.' The word 'can' covers younger players.
Subtitle 'slow spin' <- 'A normal laces drive spins about 4 turns per second' (the knuckleball, at about 0.9, is the one that almost stops).
scenes.physics_sim: Slow-motion replay: the first 0.25 s of DRIVE_R at 1/10 speed. The foot-speed bar reads from the rig.
sfx: soft pops on the target boxes
two rising whooshes for the bars

scenes.narration: First, the whip. Your thigh swings, slows, and flings your shin forward. <short pause> Then, the trampoline. The ball squashes and springs back. Your leg is way heavier, so the ball bounces off faster than your foot. <short pause> Club players your age shoot about sixty-seven kilometres an hour.
visual_beats: 'First, the whip.' X-ray leg on the teal-ink grid (#06202A, grid #0F3A47). Bones glow #C9F6FF. Label 'WHIP' pops.

'Your thigh swings, slows, and flings your shin forward.' At 1/20 speed the thigh glows pink #FF4FA3 and swings. As it slows, the pink glow fades from the thigh and a pulse of light runs down to the shin, which snaps forward. No brake icon: the leg keeps swinging through the ball. The leg morphs into a bullwhip for 0.8 s and back. The toes glow much brighter than the knee (no digits on the leg).
'Then, the trampoline.' The ball turns into a cutaway with a small trampoline inside.
'The ball squashes and springs back.' The ball flattens a few centimetres against the laces. The mat stretches, then flings. A thin timer ring fills around the ball.

'Your leg is way heavier, so the ball bounces off faster than your foot.' Inset: a heavy trolley, about four times the ball's weight, bumps a ball, which bounces off a little faster than the trolley moves. Back in X-ray, the ball leaves with a slightly longer arrow than the foot's arrow.

'Club players your age shoot about sixty-seven kilometres an hour.' A dashed ghost foot beside Tavi kicks a ghost ball. A HUD speed tag rides with the ghost ball and counts up to '≈ 67 km/h', with '≈ 42 mph' in smaller type under it. Small note: 'club players, age 12'. A tiny town car rolls along the bottom of the frame, and the ghost ball overtakes it (no speed sign, no digits).
scenes.transition_out: Pan down the X-ray leg to the ankle. A divider draws in and splits the frame in two.
facts_used: 'about sixty-seven kilometres an hour' <- 'Trained 12-year-olds kick at about 18.5 m/s at full power, 14-year-olds at about 21 m/s, and 16-year-olds at about 22.6 m/s' (18.5 m/s ≈ 67 km/h) and 'Youth shot speeds: about 67 km/h at U13, 77 km/h at U15, 81 km/h at U17'. 'Club players your age' = trained players of about 12, the U13 value. The tag rides on a ghost ball, because Tavi is 14 and his own drives run at about 78 km/h (U15).
'≈ 42 mph' (visual only) is a unit change of 67 km/h (41.6 mph) for North American viewers.
Town car (visual only, no digits, no words) is general knowledge: town speed limits are usually 50 km/h (30 mph) or lower, less than 67 km/h.

'slows' <- drive cue 'Swing from the hip, snap from the knee. Keep the knee relaxed so the thigh leads and the shin whips' and 'Do not slow the leg down before contact. Swing through the ball.' The thigh slows as the shin whips, but no one tells a player to stop the leg, so the brake icon is gone.

Toes glow brighter than the knee (visual only, no digits) <- 'At impact the toe area moves at about 22 m/s (79 km/h), but the knee moves at only about 5 m/s (17 km/h).' These are skilled-adult values, so no number is spoken or shown.
Squash (visual only) <- 'The ball squashes by about 3 to 7 cm, depending on how it is measured.'
Timer ring (visual only) <- 'Foot and ball touch for only about 9 thousandths of a second.'

'way heavier, so the ball bounces off faster than your foot' plus the trampoline follow the drive mechanism correction: the ball beats the foot only because the effective striking mass (about 1.7-2.1 kg) is several times the ball's mass AND the ball springs back. It holds for club players of 12 and up: 'the ball/foot speed ratio goes from about 1.0 at U9 to 1.26 at U20.' Whip and trampoline come before the speed, so the speed is credited to both.
Trolley at about four times the ball (visual only) <- the same 1.7-2.1 kg against a 0.43 kg ball.
sfx: low swoosh of the thigh, then a whip crack
trolley bump and a light ball tap
soft counter tick-up on the speed tag

scenes.narration: A floppy ankle is a hammer with a loose head. Some of the hit leaks away. <short pause> So: toes down, ankle locked. Hit with the middle of your laces. That's your instep. Hit near your toes, and it's about fifteen percent slower.
visual_beats: 'A floppy ankle is a hammer with a loose head.' Split screen with two X-ray ankles side by side. Left: the foot morphs into a hammer whose head hangs on a hinge.
'Some of the hit leaks away.' Left: at impact the toes are pushed further down and the hinge folds. A few orange leak puffs escape. The ball's arrow is only a little shorter than on the right.
'So: toes down, ankle locked.' Right: the toes point down, a lock icon snaps onto the ankle, and foot and shin glow as one piece. Two labels pop in order: TOES DOWN · ANKLE LOCKED.
'Hit with the middle of your laces.' A green band marks the middle of the laces. Label: MIDDLE OF LACES.
'That's your instep.' The whole laces zone glows under the green band.

WordCard: "instep" = "the laces part of your foot, not the inside". A chalk card pops on the word 'instep' beside the X-ray foot and holds 2 s. A small cross flashes over the inside of the foot on the card.

'Hit near your toes, and it's about fifteen percent slower.' The contact dot slides to the toes. A speed bar drops, with the label '−15% (toe hit)'. Floodlit inset: the slower TOE_HIT ball arrives low and late, and Chalk's diving mitten meets it. Saved. Then a ghost of the full-speed DRIVE_R slips past the same mitten into the net.
scenes.transition_out: Reverse zoom-through: pull back out of the boot to a side-on view of the pitch.
facts_used: 'about fifteen percent' <- 'The fastest spot is the middle of the laces, about 6 cm in front of the ankle joint. Contact at the toes or at the ankle gave about 15% less speed.'

Small loss on the loose-ankle side (no number spoken) <- 'In a kicking machine, a locked ankle gave about 4% more ball speed than a springy one.' The loose ankle folds toes-down, the direction given in the drive mechanism correction. The -15% label sits only on the toe-contact beat, so viewers do not mix the two.

Learn-word 'instep' (first use, WordCard) = 'the laces part of your foot, not the inside'. The narration says 'laces' first, because most coaches say 'laces' and some players use 'instep' for the inside of the foot.
Cut for the word budget: 'Chalk gets there.' The save stays on screen.
scenes.physics_sim: Inset save: TOE_HIT = 18.4 m/s (66 km/h, 15% slower than DRIVE_R), 14 deg up, 8.5 deg right. Backspin 4 rev/s, spinAxis [-0.148,-0.989,0]. Cd 0.25. It crosses about 2.7 m right of centre, about 0.35 m high, after about 1.17 s (peak about 1.45 m). That is about 0.2 s after DRIVE_R, so Chalk's dive with the same reaction delay reaches it. The full-speed ghost is DRIVE_R (s07).

scenes.narration: Your foot swings like a playground swing, flat only at the bottom. Meet the ball there. <short pause> So put your standing foot beside the ball, toes at the goal. Put it behind, and your kicking foot is already rising. Hello, car alarm. <short pause> Kicking knee and chest over the ball. Eyes on it. Strike through the middle. <short pause> The line turns slowly backward: a little backspin.
visual_beats: 'Your foot swings like a playground swing,' Side-on pitch view, Tavi at the ball. The swing arc draws from the hip and a small swing seat rides along it.
'flat only at the bottom.' A chalk dot marks the low point. A flat arrow appears there.
'Meet the ball there.' The low point slides onto the ball and the dot turns into a small target.

'So put your standing foot beside the ball, toes at the goal.' A flat disc marker lands beside the ball. A small hand icon measures the gap: one hand's width. A small arrow on the standing foot's toes points at the goal. The low point of the arc sits right at the ball.
'Put it behind, and your kicking foot is already rising.' The disc slides back and the low point moves back with it. The foot meets the ball on the way up (red arrow tilts up).
'Hello, car alarm.' A dotted ghost (the MISS path) clears the bar and drops over the fence onto a car roof. The alarm chirps and the hazard lights blink. It pays off the alarm from s01.
'Kicking knee and chest over the ball.' The disc returns. Tavi's kicking knee glows briefly, then knee and chest move over the ball and the shin stands upright.
'Eyes on it.' A thin dotted sight line runs from Tavi's eyes to the ball and holds through contact.

'Strike through the middle.' A ring target on the ball, contact at the centre. An effort bar fills almost all SPEED with only a thin SPIN sliver. After contact, Tavi lands on his kicking foot one step past the ball.
'The line turns slowly backward: a little backspin.' Tracking close-up of DRIVE_R at 1/10 speed. The line rolls slowly backward. Label: 'slow spin'.

WordCard: "backspin" = "the top of the ball turns back toward you as it flies". A chalk card pops on the word 'backspin' beside the close-up. A small arrow on the card curls backward over the top of the ball. Holds 2 s.
scenes.transition_out: The blinking hazard lights turn into the pop-in of the PracticeBoard (0.3 s swipe).
facts_used: No spoken number. 'The line turns slowly backward: a little backspin' <- 'A normal laces drive spins about 4 turns per second.' Learn-word 'backspin' (first use, WordCard), meaning from the verified jargon map: 'the top of the ball turns back toward you'.

Swing and standing-foot cue <- drive cue 'Plant the standing foot beside the ball, toes to the target, with a comfortable gap (about a boot-width to a hand-span). This puts the bottom of your swing arc at the ball, so the foot moves level at contact.' and the confirmed coaching verdict 'Plant behind = ball rises'. The hand's-width gap is shown, not spoken, for the word budget.
'Kicking knee and chest over the ball' <- drive cue 'Knee over the ball, chest over the ball at contact.' 'Eyes on it' <- drive cue 'Eyes on the ball at contact and head still.'
Landing on the kicking foot (visual only) <- volley fix 'Kick through the ball. Finish with the foot toward the target and land on the kicking foot.' It is shown, not spoken, for the word budget.
Effort bar, almost all SPEED (visual only) <- 'A computer model showed that a centre hit gives about 26 m/s with almost no spin.' No digits.
scenes.physics_sim: Ghost (standing foot behind) = MISS: 21 m/s, 18 deg up, backspin 5 rev/s, spinAxis [0,-1,0], Cd 0.25. About 3.06 m high at the goal line, lands about 30 m from the kick in the car park. Solid = DRIVE_R (see s07). Spin close-up: 4 rev/s at 1/10 speed.

scenes.narration: Classic mistake: toes up, so the ball hits your toes. Point your toes down, lock your ankle, then swing. <short pause> Solo drill: tape a line across a wall at knee height. From ten big steps, shoot ten under it. Start at half power. <short pause> Now, for real. <short pause> Chalk dives. Too late.
visual_beats: 'Classic mistake: toes up, so the ball hits your toes.' The PracticeBoard slides in with three cues: 'Run-up at an angle', 'Hand-width beside ball', 'Toes down, locked'. A pink MISTAKE stamp. A mini Tavi strikes with the toes up. The toe tip meets the ball, and the small '−15%' chip from s05 pops.
'Point your toes down, lock your ankle, then swing.' A teal FIX stamp. The toes point down and a lock clicks. Caption: 'point, lock, swing'.

'Solo drill: tape a line across a wall at knee height.' The camera pans to the concrete wall under the stand, in the same world. Tavi sticks tape across it at knee height (trim path). DRILL stamp. Board note: 'No wall? Tie a rope across a goal at knee height.' The goal safety line shows under that note.

'From ten big steps, shoot ten under it.' Tavi paces ten big steps back (tiny step counter). Each run-up starts from a slight angle. Balls thump the wall under the tape and leave hit marks. One ball rolls along the grass and its mark greys out. HUD counter ends at 7/10. Board note: 'Rollers don't count. 7 of 10? Step back. Then 5 with your other foot.'

'Start at half power.' A power meter on the board fills to half and locks. Wall safety line: 'Solid wall, no windows. Nobody near the wall. Pick a spot far from roads and parked cars. Jog and pass easy for 5 minutes. Start at half power.'
'Now, for real.' Pan back to the goal. Tavi on the 18 m spot. Chalk crouches.
'Chalk dives. Too late.' DRIVE_R skims low into the right corner. Chalk dives 12 frames late and lands flat. Net ripple and a chalk-dust puff. 1 s hold.
scenes.transition_out: The net ripple wipes across the frame. Behind it, chalk writes chapter card 2 on the grass.
facts_used: 'toes up, so the ball hits your toes' <- volley mistake 'Floppy ankle or toes up: ... Toes up also tilts the laces face upward, so the ball climbs. Toe contact gave about 15% less speed than the middle of the laces.' The -15% chip reuses the s05 fact; no number is spoken here.

'ten big steps' (about 8-10 m), 'shoot ten under it', the 7-of-10 level-up, the other-foot note and the rope note are practice instructions from the drive drill 'Knee-height target band: tape a line or hang a rope at about 50-60 cm ... From 8-12 m, drive stationary balls under the line.' They are not facts.

Run-up cue on the board <- drive cue 'Approach from an angle (about 30-45 degrees) in 3-4 steps with a longer last stride ... so the toes can point down without hitting the ground.' Hand-width cue <- 'about a boot-width to a hand-span'.
'Start at half power' and both safety lines are PracticeBoard safety rules, not facts.
Sim speed 78 km/h <- 'Youth shot speeds: about 67 km/h at U13, 77 km/h at U15, 81 km/h at U17'.
scenes.physics_sim: DRIVE_WALL (x10): from 10 m, 20 m/s (72 km/h), 5-6 deg up, backspin 4 rev/s, spinAxis [0,-1,0], Cd 0.25. It hits the wall at about 0.14-0.31 m, under the 0.5 m tape. DRIVE_R (goal): 18 m out, central. 21.7 m/s (78 km/h), 9 deg up, 8.5 deg right. Backspin 4 rev/s, spinAxis [-0.148,-0.989,0], Cd 0.25. Crosses about 2.7 m right of centre (post at 3.66 m), about 0.43 m high, after about 0.97 s. Peak about 1.0 m.

scenes.narration: Problem two. He builds a wall and guards the near post. <short pause> You need a ball that starts wide and bends back. You need sideways spin.
visual_beats: [1 s card] Chalk writes '2 · THE CURLER' on the grass, subtitle 'sideways spin'.
'Problem two.' Chalk taps his head and a small chalk light bulb pops above it.
'He builds a wall' Top-down. He drags one toe across the grass 9.15 m from the ball. The mark rises into four chalk defenders.
'and guards the near post.' Chalk shuffles to the near post. His reach bubble covers the near half of the goal. A dashed straight path from the ball hits the wall and snaps. Red cross.
'You need a ball that starts wide and bends back.' A dotted curve (CURLER preview) starts outside the far post and bends back inside it.
'You need sideways spin.' Top-view close-up of the ball. The line turns anticlockwise seen from above: its front edge swings left. Lime arrows show the same direction.
scenes.transition_out: Zoom into the inside of Tavi's boot. The X-ray foot builds, seen from above.
facts_used: No numbers. Spin direction <- verified curler note: 'A right-footer's inside-foot curler spins anticlockwise from above and bends right to left.'
Cut for the word budget: 'Chalk learns fast.' The light-bulb gag carries it.
scenes.physics_sim: Dotted preview only: CURLER samples (see s11).
sfx: chalk scrape and four soft pops for the wall

scenes.narration: New kick, new rule. Inside of your foot. This time, toes up, but the ankle stays locked: a firm, flat face. <short pause> Hit just right of centre. Wrap your foot around the ball, out to the right. Left-footed? Flip it.
visual_beats: 'New kick, new rule.' A chalk card flips from the chapter 1 laces icon to an inside-of-foot icon.
'Inside of your foot.' X-ray foot seen from above. The contact zone glows along the inside of the foot, between the big-toe joint and the inner arch.
'This time, toes up, but the ankle stays locked: a firm, flat face.' Side inset: the toes lift and turn out a little, a lock icon snaps on, and the inside of the foot shows as a flat plate.
'Hit just right of centre.' View from behind the ball. The back of the ball splits in two. The right half glows green, with the contact dot just right of the middle.

'Wrap your foot around the ball, out to the right.' One sweep arrow moves forward and to the right, toward the aim-off flag, at about 45 degrees to the foot's face. It moves one way only. It pulls the back of the ball to the right. Ultra slow motion: the ball squashes around the inner arch and leaves turning.
'Left-footed? Flip it.' The whole diagram mirrors left to right for 1 s, then flips back.
[0.5 s hold] The contact dot slides further out. An effort bar splits: SPIN grows as SPEED shrinks. Label: 'more spin, less speed'. No digits.
scenes.transition_out: Follow the spinning ball off the foot and zoom through its skin into the air around it (scale shift from boot to air, 0.8 s).
facts_used: No numbers. 'toes up, but the ankle stays locked' <- curler research cue 'Lock the ankle, toes up and slightly out ... A firm foot passes more of the swing into the ball.' 'New kick, new rule' tells viewers that the chapter 1 'toes up' mistake is about the laces drive only.
Contact zone (visual) <- curler cue 'Contact with the inside of the foot, between the big-toe joint and the inner arch.'

'just right of centre' and the sweep direction <- verified curler note (anticlockwise from above, so the back of the ball moves to the right, seen from behind). No offset in cm is spoken, per the curler correction ('a few centimetres off centre, on the far half').

'Wrap your foot around the ball' <- national FA coaching advice for the curled pass: 'wrap the kicking foot around the far side of the ball with the instep'. 'out to the right' gives the direction that the wiper picture left open.

'more spin, less speed' (label only) <- 'A computer model showed that a centre hit gives about 26 m/s with almost no spin. Moving the contact 8 cm to the side gives about 18.5 m/s and about 10 turns per second.' The spoken line 'The catch? More spin, less speed.' is cut for the word budget.

scenes.narration: Air rushes past the ball like a crowd. <short pause> The spinning ball grabs the air and flings it to one side. Throw air one way, get shoved the other way. <short pause> That's the Magnus effect: the spin push.
visual_beats: 'Air rushes past the ball like a crowd.' The Air Crowd, top view, with the ball flying toward the top of the frame. Hundreds of #7FB8FF particles with dot eyes stream from top to bottom past it.

'The spinning ball grabs the air' A thin ring of particles turns with the ball, anticlockwise, with lime spin arrows. Left side: the ring and the crowd move the same way, and the streams wrap far round the back. Right side: particles bump with small #FF4FA3 puffs and break away early.
'and flings it to one side.' The wake of swirls swings to the right. A big blue arrow labelled 'air' rides on it.
'Throw air one way,' Inset: a skateboarder throws a heavy ball to the right.

'get shoved the other way.' The skateboarder rolls left. Back on the ball, a smaller orange arrow pushes it left. A WEIGHT arrow points down beside it. The side push starts at about half its length (sim value at launch, no digits, no text).
'That's the Magnus effect: the spin push.' The orange arrow gets the label 'spin push'. Chalk pops in at the frame edge and squints at the arrows.

WordCard: "Magnus effect" = "the spin push: air shoves a spinning ball sideways, up or down". A chalk card pops on 'Magnus effect' in the top corner of the X-ray frame and holds 2.5 s. Three tiny arrows on the card point left, up and down.
scenes.transition_out: Pull back out of the air and rise past the floodlights. The night sky warms into the Open Sky palette for a top-down flight map (1.2 s).
facts_used: Direction <- verified curler mechanism note: 'The side that moves with the air separates later, the wake goes the other way, and the ball moves toward the with-flow side.' 'grabs the air and flings it to one side' is the plain version of the jargon map 'Downwash (deflected wake): the air trail thrown to one side by the spin'. 'Throw air one way, get shoved the other way' <- 'Push air one way, and the air pushes the ball the other way.' The wake story avoids the Bernoulli-only error, per the curler misconception note. The word 'drag' is not used.

Side-push arrow at about half the WEIGHT arrow (visual only, no text) <- 'The sideways push on a 19 m/s curler is about 2 newtons, roughly half the weight of the ball.' 19 m/s is an adult-level curler, not a U13 speed, so the number is no longer spoken. The arrow is the CURLER sim value at launch (about 2.1 N).

Learn-word 'Magnus effect' (first and only use, WordCard) = 'the spin push: air shoves a spinning ball sideways, up or down'. The card covers the later uses: down in s16 and up in s19. Name only; 'Magnus studied the effect in 1852' is not narrated.
Moved: 'all flight long' now lives in s11 as 'They bend about the same the whole way', so s10 ends on the term.
scenes.physics_sim: No flight. Air flow around a ball held in a 19 m/s stream, spin 7 rev/s anticlockwise seen from above. The ball flies toward the top of the frame, so the with-flow side is screen-left. The wake is drawn about 10-15 deg toward the against-flow side (a drawing value, not narrated).
sfx: soft hiss that follows the streams

scenes.narration: Curlers seem to bend late. They don't. They bend about the same the whole way. <short pause> But the gap from a straight line grows faster and faster. From twenty metres, the gap is almost three metres. <short pause> So to the keeper, it looks late.

'They don't.' The camera rises to top-down. The whole path shows as one smooth curve, a slice of a huge faint circle drawn at true scale (about 150 m across) that runs off the frame.

'They bend about the same the whole way.' A small curve gauge rides along the path. Its needle stays almost still. A small orange side-push arrow rides with the ball and stays on from the kick to the goal.

'But the gap from a straight line grows faster and faster.' A dashed launch line drops in like a ruler. Gap brackets pop at 5, 10, 15 and 20 m, each much bigger than the last (measured from the samples). The 20 m bracket splits into four copies of the 10 m bracket. The second half of the path glows: it fills about three quarters of the 20 m bracket.
'From twenty metres, the gap is almost three metres.' The last bracket gets the label '≈ 2.7 m'. A goal frame tips 90 degrees and lies beside the bracket. The bracket is longer than the goal is tall.
'So to the keeper, it looks late.' Night keeper POV: a ghost ball flies the straight line Chalk expects, and the real ball peels away late. Chalk's eyes grow 10%.
scenes.transition_out: Dive down along the curve into the night. The camera lands top-down over the floodlit pitch, on the same path.
facts_used: 'They don't. They bend about the same the whole way.' and the still curve gauge <- curler correction: 'the bend stays about the same tightness; the drift looks late mainly because of geometry'. The side-push arrow that stays on <- 'In flight, a curler lost about 22% of its speed in one second, but only about 2% of its spin.'

'grows faster and faster' and the bracket split and second-half glow (visual only) <- 'Drift grows with the square of distance. Twice the distance gives four times the drift, and about three quarters of the drift happens in the second half.'
'From twenty metres, the gap is almost three metres' <- 'A curler bends along a very large circle, about 150 m across. So a 20 m curler drifts about 2.7 m from the line it started on.'
Goal frame beside the bracket (visual only) <- 'A full-size goal is 7.32 m wide and 2.44 m high.' 2.7 m is more than the bar height (and more than the 2.13 m U11-U14 bar).
'it looks late' (no number) <- 'After the ball clears the wall, the keeper has only about 0.45 seconds.'
scenes.physics_sim: CURLER (right foot): 20 m out, left channel. 19 m/s (68 km/h), 20 deg up, 8 deg right of the target line. 7 rev/s, spinAxis [-0.063,-0.450,0.891] (tilted 63 deg from horizontal: mostly anticlockwise from above, part backspin). Cd 0.27, Cl from the kit model, spin decay 2%/s. Checks: spin push at launch about 2.1 N (about half the 4.2 N weight). Gap from the launch line about 0.7 m at 10 m and about 2.7 m at 20 m. About 2.3 m high at the 1.8 m wall at 9.15 m. Crosses the line on target after about 1.3 s at about 1.1 m. POV ghost: same launch, spin push off.
sfx: clunk as the goal frame tips

scenes.narration: From twenty metres, aim about three metres outside the far post. Point your standing foot there. Closer to goal? Aim less wide. <short pause> Classic mistake: aiming straight at the post. The spin pulls it back to Chalk. <short pause> Solo drill: put your bag halfway to the goal. Curl ten balls around it. <short pause> Starts wide. Comes home.
visual_beats: 'From twenty metres, aim about three metres outside the far post.' The PracticeBoard slides in. Top-down pitch, ball on the 20 m spot. A small flag plants itself about 2.7 m outside the far post. Board label: '≈ 3 big steps'.
'Point your standing foot there.' CUE stamp. Tavi's standing foot turns like a compass needle and points at the flag. A short launch arrow runs toward it.
'Closer to goal? Aim less wide.' The ball slides to a 10 m spot. The flag slides in to about 0.7 m outside the post.
'Classic mistake: aiming straight at the post.' MISTAKE stamp. Back at 20 m. A ghost ball launches straight at the far post.
'The spin pulls it back to Chalk.' It bends back toward the middle and crosses about 2.7 m inside the far post. Chalk steps across and catches it. A drift bracket shows the 2.7 m.

'Solo drill: put your bag halfway to the goal.' DRILL stamp. Tavi drops his kit bag at 10 m on the dashed straight line to the far post. Board note: 'Start near the edge of the box. No bag? Use a tall cone or a corner flag. Count how many go in.' Goal safety line: 'Nobody in or behind the goal. Pick a spot far from roads and parked cars. Jog and pass easy for 5 minutes. Start at half power.'
'Curl ten balls around it.' Ghost curlers pass beside the bag and bend into the goal. A fast counter ticks 1 to 10.
'Starts wide.' Behind-the-ball view. The real curler starts outside the far post and clears the chalk wall.
'Comes home.' It bends inside the far post. Chalk leans the wrong way. The net ripples and the chalk defenders crumble into dust. 1 s hold.
scenes.transition_out: The chalk dust swirls across the grass and settles as chapter card 3.
facts_used: 'From twenty metres, aim about three metres outside' <- 'a 20 m curler drifts about 2.7 m from the line it started on' and 'To land on target from 20 m, the ball must start about 7 to 8 degrees outside the target line.' 'From twenty metres' stays, because the drift is 2.7 m only at 20 m.
'Closer to goal? Aim less wide.' and the 0.7 m flag <- 'Drift grows with the square of distance. Twice the distance gives four times the drift' (2.7 m / 4 ≈ 0.7 m at 10 m).
Board label '≈ 3 big steps' is a practice unit (a big step for a 12-14-year-old is about 0.8-1 m, as in s07), not a fact.
Mistake direction <- verified curler note: the curler 'bends right to left', so a ball aimed at the far post bends back toward the middle.
Sim spin 7 rev/s <- 'University players' curlers left the foot at about 20 to 24 m/s (70 to 87 km/h) and spun 3 to 12 times each second. Most spun about 7 to 9 times.'

Drill <- curler research drill 'Pole bend gate'. The bag replaces the tall cone, because most players own a bag and flat discs, not tall cones. 'ten balls', the start spot and the count are practice instructions, not facts.
scenes.physics_sim: CURLER (s11) for the real kick. Drill ghosts: CURLER samples. The bag sits on the target line at 10 m, where the path runs about 0.7 m to its side. CURLER_AIM_MISS: same speed, angle and spin, spinAxis [0,-0.454,0.891], launched straight at the far post (0 deg). It crosses the line about 2.7 m inside the far post (toward the middle), about 1.0 m high, after about 1.34 s.

scenes.narration: Problem three. Chalk punches it clear. You pop it up off your thigh. <short pause> Now hit it before it lands.
visual_beats: [1 s card] Chalk writes '3 · THE VOLLEY' on the grass, subtitle 'forward spin'.
'Problem three. Chalk punches it clear.' Tavi shoots. Chalk punches the ball back out toward Tavi (punch_clear).
